source.attribution: CareerForge curates original practice tasks around public roadmap.sh topics. CareerForge is not affiliated with roadmap.sh.

html.title: Semantic HTML
html.focus: Document structure, forms, landmarks and meaningful elements
html.task: Build a multi-section opportunity page with a labelled application form and useful empty and error messages.
html.doneWhen: The page works without CSS, headings form a logical outline, form errors are announced and every control has a label.

css.title: Responsive CSS
css.focus: Cascade, layout, responsive sizing and visible focus
css.task: Turn the opportunity page into a responsive card layout with mobile, tablet and desktop states.
css.doneWhen: There is no horizontal overflow at 320px, text remains readable at 200% zoom and every interactive control has visible focus.

javascript.title: JavaScript foundations
javascript.focus: Functions, arrays, DOM events and asynchronous requests
javascript.task: Build a searchable opportunity list that loads JSON and handles loading, empty, success and error states.
javascript.doneWhen: Search works without a reload, failed requests offer a retry and you can explain the event and promise flow.

git.title: Git and collaboration
git.focus: Branches, commits, pull requests, diffs and conflict resolution
git.task: Build one feature on a branch, review its diff, then merge a second branch that creates a deliberate conflict.
git.doneWhen: The history is understandable, both intended changes survive and you can demonstrate reverting one commit safely.

typescript.title: Reliable TypeScript
typescript.focus: Object types, unions, narrowing, generics and strict checking
typescript.task: Model an opportunity and its loading, success and failure states with a discriminated union.
typescript.doneWhen: Strict checking passes without any or unchecked casts, and unexpected API input is validated before use.

react.title: React interface patterns
react.focus: Components, state, forms, stable identity and effect cleanup
react.task: Build a filterable learning board with add, edit, reorder and remove actions using immutable state updates.
react.doneWhen: Reordering preserves input identity, every action works from the keyboard and tests cover the main state transitions.

accessibility.title: Accessible interfaces
accessibility.focus: Keyboard use, semantics, focus management, contrast and assistive feedback
accessibility.task: Audit one flow with keyboard-only navigation and a screen reader, then repair the three highest-impact barriers.
accessibility.doneWhen: The full flow works without a pointer, focus never disappears and automated checks have no serious violations.

testing.title: Testing useful behaviour
testing.focus: Unit boundaries, integration behaviour, end-to-end flows and failure cases
testing.task: Test a critical flow at unit, integration and browser levels, including one network failure and one invalid input.
testing.doneWhen: Tests fail for the intended regression, avoid implementation details and run reliably from a clean checkout.

frontend-performance.title: Frontend performance
frontend-performance.focus: Loading cost, rendering work, image delivery and Core Web Vitals
frontend-performance.task: Profile one page, remove its largest avoidable cost and record the before and after measurement.
frontend-performance.doneWhen: The same repeatable test shows an improvement and the change preserves accessibility and expected behaviour.

web-security.title: Browser security basics
web-security.focus: Untrusted input, sessions, browser policies and dependency risk
web-security.task: Threat-model a sign-in or profile flow, then add validation and one browser security control with a regression test.
web-security.doneWhen: Trust boundaries are documented, malicious input is rejected safely and no secret reaches client code or source control.

http.title: HTTP and the web
http.focus: Requests, responses, methods, status codes, headers and caching
http.task: Inspect a real browser-to-API exchange and document the request, response, cache behaviour and failure path.
http.doneWhen: You can justify each method and status code and reproduce the exchange with a command-line client.

nodejs.title: Node.js services
nodejs.focus: Runtime fundamentals, modules, asynchronous work and server lifecycle
nodejs.task: Build a small JSON service with health, create and read endpoints plus graceful shutdown.
nodejs.doneWhen: Malformed input and missing records return consistent errors, tests pass and shutdown completes active work safely.

api-design.title: API design
api-design.focus: Resource modelling, contracts, validation, pagination and error design
api-design.task: Design and implement a versioned learning-progress API with an example contract and pagination.
api-design.doneWhen: The contract covers success and error shapes, invalid input is rejected and a breaking change is identified before release.

sql.title: Relational data and SQL
sql.focus: Schema design, joins, grouping, constraints, indexes and safe parameters
sql.task: Model learners, roadmaps and completions, then report progress including roadmaps with no activity.
sql.doneWhen: Constraints prevent invalid data, a LEFT JOIN preserves empty roadmaps and user input is always parameterized.

api-security.title: API security
api-security.focus: Authentication, authorization, rate limits, input validation and safe errors
api-security.task: Protect one private endpoint against unauthorized object access, repeated abuse and malformed input.
api-security.doneWhen: Tests prove users cannot read another account, rate limits behave predictably and responses reveal no internals.

docker.title: Containers with Docker
docker.focus: Images, containers, ports, health checks and environment configuration
docker.task: Containerize a small service with a health check and document a clean-checkout run command.
docker.doneWhen: The build is reproducible, secrets stay outside the image and the application runs as a non-root user.

spreadsheets.title: Spreadsheet analysis
spreadsheets.focus: Cleaning, formulas, lookups, validation and pivot summaries
spreadsheets.task: Clean a small outcomes dataset and build a monthly pivot summary with documented assumptions.
spreadsheets.doneWhen: Totals reconcile with source rows, duplicates and missing values are visible and formulas survive one added month.

python.title: Python for analysis
python.focus: Collections, functions, files, environments and automated tests
python.task: Write a CSV-cleaning program that normalizes categories, reports missing values and preserves rejected rows.
python.doneWhen: Tests cover empty, duplicate and malformed records and another person can run it from a clean environment.

data-cleaning.title: Data cleaning
data-cleaning.focus: Missingness, duplicates, types, outliers and reproducible transformations
data-cleaning.task: Create a reproducible cleaning notebook and a data-quality report for an intentionally messy dataset.
data-cleaning.doneWhen: Every transformation has a reason, row counts reconcile and rerunning from raw data produces the same result.

statistics.title: Practical statistics
statistics.focus: Distributions, sampling, uncertainty, correlation and experiment basics
statistics.task: Answer one product question with descriptive statistics and a confidence interval, then explain the limitations.
statistics.doneWhen: The method matches the data, uncertainty is visible and the conclusion avoids causal claims the evidence cannot support.

data-visualization.title: Data visualization
data-visualization.focus: Chart choice, scales, annotation, accessibility and truthful comparison
data-visualization.task: Create three views of the same dataset, select the clearest one and document why the others mislead or distract.
data-visualization.doneWhen: The chart answers one stated question, labels work without colour and scales do not exaggerate the result.

dashboard.title: Decision-ready dashboards
dashboard.focus: Information hierarchy, filters, metric definitions and operational context
dashboard.task: Build a one-page outcomes dashboard for a named decision-maker and a single recurring decision.
dashboard.doneWhen: Metrics are defined, filters are understandable, empty states are useful and the intended decision can be made quickly.

data-storytelling.title: Data storytelling
data-storytelling.focus: Audience, narrative, evidence, uncertainty and recommendations
data-storytelling.task: Turn an analysis into a five-slide briefing with one decision, three findings and one explicit limitation.
data-storytelling.doneWhen: Every claim traces to evidence, uncertainty is stated and the recommendation is proportionate to the result.

data-ethics.title: Responsible data use
data-ethics.focus: Privacy, consent, representation, bias and appropriate retention
data-ethics.task: Review a dataset for collection risk, missing populations and harmful proxy variables before analysis.
data-ethics.doneWhen: The review records what should not be used, who may be harmed and one concrete mitigation or stop condition.

ux-research.title: User research foundations
ux-research.focus: Research questions, interviews, observation and evidence synthesis
ux-research.task: Plan and run three short interviews about one real workflow, using neutral prompts and consent.
ux-research.doneWhen: Notes separate observation from interpretation and findings include supporting evidence, limits and open questions.

user-flows.title: User flows and journeys
user-flows.focus: Goals, entry points, decisions, recovery and end states
user-flows.task: Map the current and improved journey for completing one high-value task, including failure and recovery paths.
user-flows.doneWhen: The flow has one clear goal, no unexplained dead ends and every branch ends in success, recovery or an honest stop.

information-architecture.title: Information architecture
information-architecture.focus: Mental models, grouping, labels, navigation and findability
information-architecture.task: Run a small card sort, propose a navigation model and test five findability tasks with fresh participants.
information-architecture.doneWhen: Labels use user language, results identify confusion and revisions connect directly to observed failures.

figma.title: Figma and interface craft
figma.focus: Auto layout, reusable components, constraints, variants and interaction states
figma.task: Design a responsive opportunity-search flow with reusable controls and loading, empty and error states.
figma.doneWhen: Components resize without manual repair, variants are named consistently and the prototype covers keyboard focus order.

interaction-design.title: Interaction design
interaction-design.focus: Feedback, constraints, state changes, motion and error prevention
interaction-design.task: Prototype a multi-step flow and document the feedback shown after every important user action.
interaction-design.doneWhen: Users always know what changed, destructive actions are recoverable and motion has a reduced-motion alternative.

design-systems.title: Design systems
design-systems.focus: Tokens, component anatomy, variants, documentation and governance
design-systems.task: Create a small token set and three documented components that cover real product states.
design-systems.doneWhen: Names express purpose, components handle disabled and error states and documentation includes when not to use them.

usability-testing.title: Usability testing
usability-testing.focus: Task design, facilitation, severity and evidence-led iteration
usability-testing.task: Test a prototype with five task-based sessions and rank findings by frequency and impact.
usability-testing.doneWhen: Prompts avoid coaching, evidence supports each issue and the top revision is tested again rather than assumed fixed.

handoff.title: Design-to-development handoff
handoff.focus: States, responsive behaviour, content rules, acceptance criteria and collaboration
handoff.task: Prepare one feature for implementation with annotated states, responsive rules and testable acceptance criteria.
handoff.doneWhen: A developer can identify every state and edge case without guessing and open questions are resolved in writing.

portfolio-case-study.title: Evidence-led case study
portfolio-case-study.focus: Problem framing, individual contribution, evidence, iteration and outcomes
portfolio-case-study.task: Publish a concise case study that shows what changed because of research or testing, including one failed direction.
portfolio-case-study.doneWhen: Claims are supported, your role is explicit, confidential details are removed and limitations are honest.

linux.title: Linux foundations
linux.focus: Files, processes, permissions, services, logs and shell automation
linux.task: Provision a least-privilege service user, run a small service and diagnose an intentional startup failure from logs.
linux.doneWhen: The service restarts predictably, permissions are minimal and the diagnosis is captured as a repeatable runbook.

networking.title: Networking foundations
networking.focus: DNS, addresses, ports, TLS, routing and common failure modes
networking.task: Trace a request from DNS lookup to TLS connection and simulate one DNS and one port failure.
networking.doneWhen: You can locate each failure with standard tools and explain which layer owns the repair.

ci-cd.title: Continuous delivery
ci-cd.focus: Build checks, artifacts, environments, safe releases and rollback
ci-cd.task: Create a pipeline that tests, builds and deploys a small service only after required checks pass.
ci-cd.doneWhen: A broken test blocks release, secrets stay in the platform store and a documented rollback restores the prior version.

cloud.title: Cloud fundamentals
cloud.focus: Compute, storage, identity, networking, regions and cost awareness
cloud.task: Deploy a small service with least-privilege access, a budget alert and a diagram of its trust boundaries.
cloud.doneWhen: The service is reproducible, public access is intentional and idle resources can be identified and removed.

observability.title: Observability
observability.focus: Structured logs, useful metrics, traces, service objectives and actionable alerts
observability.task: Instrument one request path and create an alert for a user-visible failure rather than raw infrastructure noise.
observability.doneWhen: A test incident can be traced end to end and the alert includes context, ownership and a useful runbook.

infrastructure-security.title: Infrastructure security
infrastructure-security.focus: Least privilege, secrets, patching, network exposure and audit trails
infrastructure-security.task: Review a small deployment for excessive access and replace one long-lived secret with a safer mechanism.
infrastructure-security.doneWhen: Permissions are justified, secret rotation is tested and changes leave an auditable record without leaking sensitive values.

incident-response.title: Incident response
incident-response.focus: Triage, communication, mitigation, recovery and blameless learning
incident-response.task: Run a tabletop outage, write a timestamped incident record and test the highest-value follow-up action.
incident-response.doneWhen: Roles and escalation are clear, recovery is verifiable and the follow-up fixes a system weakness rather than blaming a person.

tracks.title: Frontend Developer
tracks.audience: For learners who want to build accessible, responsive web interfaces.
tracks.outcome: Ship a tested interface that works across devices and failure states.

phases.title: Build the web foundation
phases.goal: Understand the platform before adding framework complexity.

phases.title: Engineer real interfaces
phases.goal: Turn requirements into maintainable and inclusive product states.

phases.title: Ship with confidence
phases.goal: Prove behaviour, measure speed and protect user trust.

capstone.title: Accessible opportunity explorer
capstone.brief: Build and deploy a responsive opportunity search app with filters, saved items and complete loading, empty and error states.
capstone.proof: Publish the code, a live URL, keyboard and accessibility notes, tests for a critical flow and one before/after performance measurement.

tracks.title: Backend Developer
tracks.audience: For learners who want to design dependable APIs and data services.
tracks.outcome: Deliver a secure, tested and containerized API with a clear contract.

phases.title: Understand the request path
phases.goal: Learn how web requests, code and version control fit together.

phases.title: Build a data service
phases.goal: Create a clear server boundary backed by relational data.

phases.title: Make it dependable
phases.goal: Test failure, enforce access rules and package a repeatable runtime.

capstone.title: Learning progress API
capstone.brief: Build a private API for roadmaps, progress and evidence with pagination, ownership rules and useful error responses.
capstone.proof: Publish an API contract, automated tests for authorization and invalid input, a container run guide and a small threat model.

tracks.title: Full-Stack Developer
tracks.audience: For learners who want to own a feature from interface to database.
tracks.outcome: Ship one complete, secure product flow across browser, API and data layers.

phases.title: Learn the whole request
phases.goal: Build strong browser and collaboration fundamentals.

phases.title: Connect interface and data
phases.goal: Model a typed UI, service boundary and relational store.

phases.title: Prepare for production
phases.goal: Design the contract, test risk and package a safe release.

capstone.title: Career application workspace
capstone.brief: Build a responsive app that saves opportunities, tracks status changes and protects each learner's private records.
capstone.proof: Publish the live flow, schema and API contract, browser and authorization tests, an accessibility review and a deployment runbook.

tracks.title: Data Analyst
tracks.audience: For learners who want to turn imperfect data into responsible decisions.
tracks.outcome: Produce a reproducible analysis and a decision-ready dashboard.

phases.title: Query and calculate
phases.goal: Use the core tools that analysts meet in real teams.

phases.title: Clean and reason
phases.goal: Make transformations reproducible and conclusions proportionate.

phases.title: Communicate a decision
phases.goal: Turn evidence into a clear, responsible product for an audience.

capstone.title: Opportunity outcomes study
capstone.brief: Clean and analyze an anonymized applications dataset, then build a dashboard for improving one part of the learner journey.
capstone.proof: Publish raw-to-clean transformations, metric definitions, the dashboard, a five-slide briefing and a privacy and limitation note.

tracks.title: UX Designer
tracks.audience: For learners who want to turn user evidence into inclusive product decisions.
tracks.outcome: Research, prototype and validate a complete flow with a credible case study.

phases.title: Understand the problem
phases.goal: Replace assumptions with a grounded model of people and tasks.

phases.title: Design the experience
phases.goal: Create responsive, inclusive states that communicate clearly.

phases.title: Prove and communicate
phases.goal: Test the work, prepare implementation and show honest evidence.

capstone.title: Learning-plan redesign
capstone.brief: Research and redesign a confusing learning roadmap so a first-time learner can choose, start and understand a path.
capstone.proof: Publish the research plan, current and revised flow, accessible prototype, usability findings, developer handoff and concise case study.

tracks.title: DevOps Engineer
tracks.audience: For learners who want to make delivery reliable, observable and safe.
tracks.outcome: Operate a repeatable deployment with useful alerts and a tested recovery path.

phases.title: Understand the system
phases.goal: Diagnose the operating system, network and change history.

phases.title: Automate delivery
phases.goal: Package, verify and release a service repeatably.

phases.title: Operate with confidence
phases.goal: See failure, reduce exposure and recover deliberately.

capstone.title: Production-ready service path
capstone.brief: Deploy a containerized service through CI/CD with least privilege, actionable telemetry and a recovery exercise.
capstone.proof: Publish infrastructure notes, passing pipeline evidence, an alert and runbook, a cost check and a short incident retrospective.
